# Phyllum

> A design system companion that turns prose, images, or the styles already in a codebase into named tokens and components, all recorded in one file.

Phyllum writes exactly one file in a user's codebase: `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`. Every command is
rerunnable and converges — re-assessing doesn't duplicate tokens, re-creating a component
opens a revision. `assess` reads the codebase, `tokenise` reads a sentence, `create` reads
intent. Mechanical commands run in pure Node; the intelligent ones (`create`,
`tokenise`) run natively inside a Claude Code session or shell out to the `claude` CLI.
These paths are repo-relative; this repo has no published remote yet.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what Phyllum is, how to install it, how it works
- [Skill definition](skill/SKILL.md): the router — commands, the file format, the two rules that outrank being helpful. Start here to change behaviour.
- [CLI entry point](bin/phyllum.js): argument parsing and the single call into execute; the terminal surface
- [File template](templates/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md): the canonical DESIGN-SYSTEM.md skeleton every install scaffolds

## Reference

- [create](skill/refs/create.md): the three modes (prose, image, pick), archetype contracts, the follow-up loop, acceptance and the write step
- [assess](skill/refs/assess.md): the read-only codebase scan — what is read (including every text file, in any language), React-only component detection, clustering before naming, the diff on rerun
- [tokenise](skill/refs/tokenise.md): naming one value from one sentence — the three passes, the naming scales, the follow-up loop, acceptance
- [init](skill/refs/init.md): the guided setup walkthrough — scaffold, skill install, optional seeding
- [gui](skill/refs/gui.md): the localhost server contract and the three-view dashboard
- [system](skill/refs/system.md): the terminal listing format
- [version](skill/refs/version.md): the installed version, the on-demand npm registry check, and what happens offline
- [update](skill/refs/update.md): install detection (npm/pnpm, global/project), the graceful refusals, and the skill re-sync
